title: PHP Memory Limit Exhausted
description: Fix 'Allowed memory size exhausted' fatal errors — tune limits, find memory-hungry plugins, and optimize queries.

steps.title: Identify When Memory Errors Occur
steps.instructions: Check debug.log for the exact file and line. Note if errors happen on specific pages, during cron, imports, or plugin updates.

steps.title: Raise WordPress Memory Constants
steps.instructions: Add define('WP_MEMORY_LIMIT', '256M') and define('WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT', '512M') to wp-config.php. Confirm php.ini memory_limit is at least as high.

steps.title: Profile Memory Usage on Staging
steps.instructions: Use Query Monitor or similar to see which plugins consume the most memory per request. Focus fixes on the top offenders.

steps.title: Reduce Autoloaded Options Bloat
steps.instructions: Large autoloaded options load on every request. Audit wp_options for oversized autoload=yes rows and fix or remove orphaned plugin data.

steps.title: Deactivate Unused or Duplicate Plugins
steps.instructions: Page builders, SEO suites, and backup plugins are common memory hogs. Remove plugins not actively needed on production.

steps.title: Enable Object Caching
steps.instructions: Persistent object cache lowers memory churn from repeated option and post meta lookups. Verify Redis/Memcached is active after install.

steps.title: Verify Stable Operation
steps.instructions: Load high-traffic pages and run previously failing actions. Monitor logs for 48 hours to ensure memory errors do not return.
